title: Predictive soft-shedder using short-term heatmaps and SLO-credit accounting
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a predictive, tenant-aware "soft-shedder" that uses short-term request heatmaps and per-tenant SLO credit accounting to make admission decisions and drive graceful degradation. Goal: reduce catastrophic tail-latency spikes during regional overloads while preserving high-value requests and minimizing user-visible correctness regressions. This feature complements existing priority lanes by adding a time-series predictor + SLO-credit budget that can pre-emptively throttle or degrade responses rather than hard-dropping requests.
acceptance_criteria: Predictive heatmap model runs in runtime path with <=2ms median overhead on a 32-concurrent request host
Per-tenant SLO-credit ledger persists across failover and is readable by the admission controller within 50ms
System reduces p99 latency by >=15% during synthetic spikes while maintaining >=95% success rate for top-tier tenants in the canary region
Graceful degradation ladder implemented: response-slimming -> output-truncation -> model-variant fallback -> reject, with configured tunable thresholds
Automated integration tests for admission decisions and degradations covering at least 80% of code paths
tasks: Design SLO-credit model (credit accrual, spend rate, decay) and document in Confluence
Prototype short-term heatmap predictor using exponential windowed counters (host-level + tenant-level)
Integrate predictor into admission controller and expose decision metrics
Implement graceful degradation ladder hooks in response pipeline
Add durable ledger (Redis + WAL) for tenant SLO credits and test multi-region failover read/write semantics
Write unit/integration tests and load test scenarios replicating multi-region spike
Create console dashboard for SLO-credit balances, heatmaps, and admission events
Prepare rollout canary with 5% traffic in staging -> 1 region -> multi-region
Author runbook for operators describing failure modes and rollback steps
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature flag behind 'predictive-soft-shed' and 'slo-credit' (dev env only)
Phase 1: Internal staging canary (5% of internal traffic) for 1 week
Phase 2: Public canary in a single region (5% production traffic) + intensive load test
Phase 3: Gradual ramp to 25% across two regions with monitoring and abort conditions
Phase 4: Full enablement with default conservative parameters; tune over 4 weeks
Rollback: disable flag, drain admission caches, revert ledger write mode to read-only
monitoring: Alerts: p99 latency spike >20% over baseline for 10m, sudden credit depletion for >5% of tenants
Dashboard: per-tenant credit time series, admission rate, degradation ladder counts
SLO observability: correlate credit spends with served request quality via sampled traces
implementation_notes: Heatmap design: 1s/5s/30s buckets aggregated per host, per-region, per-tenant. Use compact ring counters to bound memory
Predictor: lightweight AR(1) style predictor + anomaly detector; experimental ML model deferred to follow-up
SLO-credit policy: accrue credits proportional to unused budget; top-tier tenants get reserved baseline credits
Degradation ladder: prefer fidelity-preserving operations (response-slimming, content-prioritization) before switching model variants
Telemetry: sample 1% of degraded responses with full token traces for quality regression analysis
Multi-region: ledger writes are local-first with async cross-region reconciliation and conflict-resolution by highest-balance-wins for short windows
